criteria.reason: Most of the essay speaks in a reflective, first-person-plural 'we' voice ('I think many of us...', 'What I've started noticing...') rather than issuing moral commands, which keeps it largely free of overt preaching. The instructional 'Building the Anvil' section reads as mechanical steps ('Perform a total brain dump...', 'Assign these Big Rocks...') rather than sermonizing. However, the closing binary ('you can continue to play whack-a-mole with your life until you burn out, or you can build an Anvil') and the terse moral coda ('Responsibility begins with the calendar.') edge toward preachy ultimatum framing, which slightly undercuts an otherwise measured tone.
